# Closing a dashboard popup duplicates its returned widget

## Context

The operator reported a distinct Fleet Manager Accounts failure on 2026-10-08: tear the pane into a popup, close that popup, observe an empty source view, navigate to another left-rail view and back, then see two Accounts panels stacked.

This is independent of the overly broad body drag handle tracked in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#601. A legitimate header tear-out must return correctly too.

Installed witness: Institution `fd958fba1e7d492a5ae2b9b283df1f65e5cc1a6e`, Engine `82bc6158444306e0c342e8cda480e77158c9fedb`. Read-only Neural Link verification after the reported sequence finds **one Accounts instance**, present **twice each** in its source dashboard's `items`, VDOM and DOM; `detachedItems.size === 0`. The window log records the child disconnect/re-integration, followed by navigation away/back and a wedged viewport update. The installed observation is distinct from the isolated browser attribution below.

## The Problem

Closing the popup neither immediately restores a usable source pane nor preserves unique membership through navigation. The duplicated rendering must not be hidden with a restart or a second instance.

Design authority: `src/dashboard/Container.mjs` class JSDoc promises that a manually closed detached window has its widget “correctly reclaimed and restored to the dashboard”.

## The Architectural Reality

This is the legacy `Neo.dashboard.Container` lifecycle used by Accounts, not the cockpit's newer DockLayout. At reproduction baseline Engine `994fa3e6d87a132ac8c46e3f6b08b969e55aab55`:

- `onWindowConnect()` adds the widget to the popup with `removeFromPreviousParent = !#isWindowDragging`.
- `onWindowDisconnect()` returns through `me.insert(index, widget)`.
- `src/container/Base.mjs#insert` only early-returns for the same parent at the same index; otherwise it inserts the instance and its VDOM.

A 2026-10-08 isolated Node probe now confirms the retained-membership mechanism using real Dashboard, container and component instances plus the unit runtime, with only window admission/URL seams stubbed. Held tear-out → connect → terminal drop/end → disconnect leaves two source items and two VDOM references to the original widget, drains the popup and clears the detached map. The ordinary (non-drag) popup control removes the source slot on connect and returns exactly one item/reference at its original index. A repeated disconnect adds nothing further. The [browser repair receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19462#issuecomment-6050563648) additionally isolates the initially blank return: ordinary removal queues an update for the closed popup, and coalesced source remove/reinsert leaves the source vnode believing its missing DOM node exists.

## The Fix

Repair manual-close return in the owning dashboard lifecycle so the original component reattaches exactly once, with coherent parent/window/render state. Reuse existing container ownership primitives; avoid a second Accounts instance or consumer-side duplicate filtering. Add regression coverage to the existing dashboard tests and a browser journey through popup close and source hide/show.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy dashboard popup-close return | Dashboard class restoration contract | Original widget restored once immediately; navigation preserves it | Existing refusal/cleanup paths retain recoverable ownership | Existing lifecycle JSDoc | Component identity and item/VDOM/DOM counts, plus browser close-and-return journey |

Decision Record impact: none; restoration of the existing lifecycle contract. Owning files already exist in Engine; no new service or public API is required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A normal header tear-out followed by manual popup close restores the original view without navigation or app restart.
- [ ] Source dashboard `items`, VDOM and DOM each contain the widget exactly once, with source parent/window ownership and no stale detached entry.
- [ ] Navigate away and back, then repeat tear-out/close: still one usable pane with its selection/state retained.
- [ ] Coverage exposes the retained-membership duplicate on the unfixed path and passes with the repair, including close/update ordering relevant to the initially empty view.
- [ ] Existing dashboard drag-back reintegration remains functional.
- [ ] Post-merge installed acceptance on the next authorized FM candidate records the header drag, close, immediate return and navigation checks separately from source/CI results.

## Out of Scope

Body drag admission (Institution `#601`), global DockLayout refactoring, migration/restart of peer harnesses, and an app install without its own boundary.

Intake: **Prescription checked: `src/dashboard/Container.mjs` — owns the concern.** It retains the source slot during the held popup transfer and must retire that reservation before ordinary reinsertion. Broadening generic `Base.insert()` deduplication would conceal the inconsistent owner state.

The isolated real-instance pair reproduces the duplicate only on the retained-slot path. Prior Memory Core reasoning (`2552b73a-8f6a-41e9-8e4a-98860dd9ee57`, `cf518c0b-3122-48b1-bcdb-de08b3570981`, session `eb28ff77-137c-4626-8e5f-3f8f29d85cfc`) identifies the same historical return concern and rejects changing connect behavior or destroying the widget. Current source and the new probe supply the present-tense evidence.

Implementation begins with a regression using real container ownership operations, covering both retained and absent source slots. Browser close/hide/show validation remains necessary for the initially blank paint; no installed acceptance is claimed by the Node probe.

### @neo-gpt-sophie - 2026-10-08T01:54:26Z

### Browser and ownership receipt

The isolated legacy-dashboard browser journey reproduces the operator's initially blank return, including the same wedged popup-viewport warning. Three stages are required in the disconnect owner:

1. Remove the widget from the closed popup silently; a normal removal queues a render for the departed window.
2. Retire the source's retained sorting reservation. If the source is mounted, await that removal's render acknowledgement: remove-and-insert in one batch otherwise leaves a vnode that still believes the missing DOM node exists.
3. Insert the original widget once. Coalesce repeated disconnects per detached entry and preserve a newer admission across the await.

Final `LegacyPopupReturnNL.spec.mjs` uses the existing dashboard example with a configured header handle and an existing empty shared-worker popup host. Real pointer gestures and physical `beforeunload` close pass: **two immediate visible returns, one close while the source is hidden followed by show, hide/show consistency after each cycle, retained body content, and drag-back reintegration**. Items, VDOM and DOM agree; the original identity and source window return. This is local browser evidence, not an installed FM cut.

Real-instance units expose the original duplicate and the attempted closed-window update. The focused suite passes **11/11**, including an in-flight duplicate disconnect and a newer admission while removal is awaiting acknowledgement. Full units pass **4,843 with 2 skipped**. An earlier full run had one unrelated reporter assertion false positive: PID text `4101` matched `loadAverage: 4.17041015625`; the launch-exit array correctly contained only PID 4102. That raw defect note is retained, the reporter spec passes 11/11 alone, and no reporter code was changed here.

Post-merge installed acceptance remains on neomjs/neo-agent-institution#12. Header-only Accounts admission remains independently tracked in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#601.
